newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea said intervening, sells dollars.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea said intervening, sells dollars.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened in interbank market in late Monday trading, selling dollars at around 855.00 won per dollar, to slow the local currency's fall, dealers said.
The won was trading at 854.80 shortly after the central bank's dollar-selling intervention. It opened trading at 854.60 and moved in a relatively narrow range from 854.50 to 855.00.
Dealers said the local currency had been pressured by the nation's snowballing trade deficit and speculation that its downward trend would hold on for a considerable period.
